Both ABIs contain no warnings, notes, errors, or fatal diagnostics. Missing, changed, duplicated, reordered, or extra source markers, compile commands, link arguments, diagnostics, pipeline markers, version markers, or success frames fail closed.

Resolver metadata declares GPLv2, display version v0.9.38.7, and pce|cue|ccd|chd|toc|m3u content while both binaries report v1.31.0.0. That version discrepancy requires operator review. Any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate; corresponding-source and license obligations must be reviewed before publication.

No firmware or BIOS is packaged. PCE-CD content requires a legally supplied external system-card BIOS; resolver metadata declares four optional candidates and recommends syscard3.pce with MD5 38179df8f4ac870017db21ebcbf53114. HuCard and BIOS-backed CD loading, controls, audio and video pacing, saves, deterministic states, frontend integration, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates.

PCE Fast trades compatibility for speed and upstream warns that some games do not work. It does not support SuperGrafx games; where performance permits, the non-Fast or other PCE-compatible cores may provide broader compatibility. Native HuCard, PCE-CD, CHD, multi-disc, incompatibility, and SuperGrafx boundary behavior remain unvalidated on target devices.

The software-only Unix recipe produces one shared artifact per ABI and provides no evidence for device-specific duplicate builds. ARM64 reaches GLIBC 2.27 and is build-identity-bound only to ra64-universal-v1; ARMHF is bound only to ra32-a30-v1.
